There are several performance models that you can use for recognizing text lines in an image. Here are a few popular ones:

1.   
    
    __Region of Interest (ROI) based Models__: These models use ROI coordinates to specify the location of the text in the image. Examples include MSER (Maximally Stable Extremal Regions) and TextBoxes.
    
    
2.   
    
    __Text-based Models__: These models use text-based representations, such as character-level or word-level features, to recognize text. Examples include RNN-based models, such as Encoder-Decoder models, and CNN-based models, such as TextNet.
    
    
3.   
    
    __Object Detection-based Models__: These models use object detection frameworks, such as Faster R-CNN or RetinaNet, to recognize text. Examples include Text-Focused Object Detection and Text-based Object Detection.
    
    
4.   
    
    __Text-to-Image Generation-based Models__: These models generate an image from a text description, and use the generated image to recognize text. Examples include Text-to-Image Generation with Deep Residual Learning.
    
    

The choice of model depends on the specific requirements of your application, such as the complexity of the text, the size and quality of the input images, the computational resources available, and the accuracy required. It's important to evaluate the performance of different models on your specific dataset and evaluate which one is best suited for your use case.
